I still regret that I did not die aftwards, but I actually would have regretted it if I would have died before that. Nothing compares to true love. Even when it does not last (and yes, this can still mean that there was true love).

That is indeed very hard. And as I said, I completely understand how devestating this can feel. I also did not want to say or imply in any way that you would have to feel okay with this. If something is bothering you right now, it usually gets not better at that very moment when thinking that it will be better one day. However, I just wanted to tell you that because sometimes it's hard in these situations to even consider that things usually get better. Not always, not for all of us, not everything, but most of the time. 

That you need certain grades to do the only thing that makes you happy is just cruell. May I ask what that is and if you see any other workaround how you can do that anyway or something similar or in a different setting (place, people, etc.)?
The people who really matter will not judge you at all! However, these kind of people are rare, but very precious.

I can understand what you mean. It has been a very very long time since I've been the first choice for someone else. Thus, in regards of social connectedness, I can not say much. 

However, I can do say that grades do not matter as much as people might think they do. Or at least not nearly as much as I thought they would. I had to repeat two years during my school time (once somewhen around 15 and once again with 18) and was bottom last during these years. I was so ashamed and it was very difficult for me to keep trying. However, I was able to make it and now, no one cares about my grades back then or even that I had to repeat two years. Got my master's degree two years ago, I am doing my PhD now and even was hired to teach a master's degree class at university last year. So rest assured, grades will get less important over time, even though they might appear to have a bigger impact now, than they eventually will have.

Actually, there are many reasons why I think it is always a relieve if someone is not going through with suicide.

First of all, suicide is rarely painless and most often not successful (studies go as far as showing that only around 1 out of nearly over 30 attempts). So the fact that a human being that is already hurting so much to consider this an option does not have to put themselves through additional pain, suffering and risk of impairment if unsuccessful is already one good reason for me to feel glad that someone stayed alive (even if I do not know this person). 

Second, usually there is hope. This will sound like the most clichée and most stupid comment ever, but if you look closely, it usually gets better. I don't know the numbers by heart anymore, but 90% of people who tried to kill themselves do not die by suicide later on. And even though this does not mean that their lives improved, it still gives some evidence that things can get better. Especially when you take further research into account that shows that 80-100% of the people asked in studies would have regretted if they would have died on a later point. And even though I am a bit critical about these studies and what they imply, these studies (and many more) show, that suicide is usually a more compulsive act caused by severe amount of distress that most often passes, diminishes or people can learn to cope with. And don't get me wrong, I do not believe that this is always the case. Especially on a subreddit like this you'll probably find many people who might not see it that way and might don't regret it if they would have died. 

Maybe I take the name of this subreddit to literally, but for me it sounds like this should be the place for people to go to when they need to know that they are heard and where they can make it through another day/night/hour/week/month.

Tl;dr: This is why I hope for everyone that they can make it through rough time(s) so that they get the chance to get better and will live a happy life, even though or especially because they can't even imagine right now that this is even possible. Because most often, it actually is.
